solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spot boy not entirely ready initially

indicators.note: something not entirely there is incomplete, so the final letter is cut away

parts.note: Cornel is a boy's name, as in the actor Cornel Wilde

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone notices a lad who is not quite prepared at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Spot reads as a verb meaning notice, but it is a noun, as in a tight spot. The boy is the actor Cornel Wilde's first name, an uncommon one solvers rarely think of.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a tight corner and being in a tight spot are the same awkward situation, so the words are synonyms here.

clue.text: Leading couples in court meet and support return to former position

indicators.note: leading couples are the front pairs, so the first two letters of each word are kept

parts.note: the leading pair of letters of the word, an operation not an abbreviation
the leading pair of letters of the word, an operation not an abbreviation
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Dancers or tennis pairs gather on court, backing a player returning to their old rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'couples' are pairs of letters, not people: the first two of court and of meet, followed by a word for support.
explanation.definitionFit: A comeback is a recovery of an earlier standing, as when a retired athlete or faded star wins back status.

clue.text: Dazzling new present with advance inside?

indicators.note: paired with inside, this says one word sits within the other
inside places one word within the other, splitting it
a new version of a word is a remade one, so its letters come in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: A dazzling new gift arrives with a cash advance tucked inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' reads as a gift, and 'advance' as a cash loan; the question mark admits the surface is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resplendent is splendid and brilliantly shining, which matches the sense of dazzling in appearance.

clue.text: Your race on water, they say, for money?

indicators.note: what they say is what is spoken, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: a race on water is a row, so 'your row' said quickly gives the sound

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether your rowing race is being run for prize money.
explanation.walkthrough: A row is a boat race; spoken as 'your row', the two words run together into the name of a currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency shared by many European Union countries, so it is a kind of money.

clue.text: Shows worry about airline tickets after vacation

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is wrapped round another

parts.note: care is anxiety or worry
BA is British Airways

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A traveller frets over flight tickets once the holiday is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Shows reads as a verb, but it is a plural noun. 'Vacation' looks like a holiday but means emptying out the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub entertainment of songs and sketches, so cabarets are kinds of stage shows.

clue.text: Correctness of account supported by religious office

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported means sitting on top, so the first word comes above the second

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
a curacy is the post held by a curate

explanation.surface: A church office vouches for the correctness of a set of accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: A curate is an assistant priest in the Church of England, and the curacy is his or her office.
explanation.definitionFit: Accuracy is the quality of being exact and free of error, which is what correctness describes.

clue.text: Expert on star — more flexible

indicators.note: something flexible bends into other shapes, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A specialist on a celebrity is said to be more adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert on star' wants to be the whole definition, but only 'Expert' defines; 'on star more' is the material, and the surface hints at the answer's field.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer is a scientific specialist, a person with expert knowledge of stars and planets.

clue.text: Period in Copper Age

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the following words, spanning the gap

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A history lesson names a stage within the Copper Age.
explanation.walkthrough: The Copper Age is itself a period, which makes the surface feel like a straight definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a distinct span of history, so it is a period of time in the same sense.

clue.text: Coy about slip in drink?

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is wrapped round another

parts.note: coy and shy both mean bashful
to err is to slip up

explanation.surface: Someone is bashful about a blunder made while drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the link here, joining the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain, so it is one kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Code word for a dominant person

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word used for the letter A in the radio spelling alphabet
second meaning: the leading member of a group

explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' at the end looks like a throwaway article; it is the letter A that the code word stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: The NATO phonetic alphabet spells A this way, and the top animal in a pack is likewise called the alpha.

clue.text: Recalling some classical arts, impressive feature of southwest Europe

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters are read backwards
some means only part, so a run of letters is taken from inside the words

parts.note: a run spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A writer recalls classical culture as a striking part of southern Europe's heritage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressive feature' reads as one phrase, but the adjective only lends its first two letters. The mistral is a strong cold wind blowing down the Rhône valley in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a powerful regional wind of southern France, a notable weather characteristic of that corner of Europe.

clue.text: Small house, somewhere to sleep time and time again?

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
T is the abbreviation for time
an age is a long time; 'and' just carries on the list

explanation.surface: A cosy little house where someone can sleep over again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time and time again' looks like an idiom for repeatedly, but time is used twice: once as a letter, once as a longer span.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a modest dwelling, typically in the countryside, so it is a little house by definition.

clue.text: Call good-looker, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken aloud, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: Someone is told to phone the attractive person they keep hearing about.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, to give someone a bell is to phone them.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a bell is a telephone call, as in 'give me a bell later', so the noun matches call.

clue.text: More cautious about remote, half-forgotten, driver from past

indicators.note: forgetting half of something drops that share of its letters
about means around, so one word is wrapped round another

parts.note: chary means cautious, so charier is more cautious
the second half of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: A wary viewer half forgets the TV remote, like some old-time driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' suggests a TV controller, but it only supplies its back half.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer drove a horse-drawn chariot in ancient races and battles, so he was a driver of former times.

clue.text: Retail again stirring — just

indicators.note: stirring mixes things around, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Shops are just starting to stir back into life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like the adverb 'only', but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An egalitarian approach treats all people as equals, which is a fair and even-handed one.

clue.text: Good for you, nice ale? Fib, unfortunately!

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub boast that a nice pint is healthy is sadly exposed as a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and exclamation break the clue into a little exchange, hiding that the middle words are pure letter material.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneficial does you good, bringing health or advantage, so the phrase is a direct paraphrase.

clue.text: Communicate argument against valuing every year from the outset

parts.note: a con is a point against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone voices an objection to valuing things annually from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argument against' reads as a whole phrase about opposition; it is just the short noun from pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: To convey an idea is to get it across to someone, which is what communicating does.

clue.text: One studying Church participating in type of panel

indicators.note: to participate in something is to be inside it, so one word goes within another

parts.note: a solar panel
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A student of the Church sits on some kind of panel discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panel' suggests a committee, but the type meant is the solar panel on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or student engaged in academic study, so is one who studies.

clue.text: Self-indulgent in 1960s maybe, nihilist — extremely

parts.note: the 1960s are an example of a ten-year span

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters at either end

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A hedonist from the swinging Sixties turns out to be a thoroughgoing nihilist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the 1960s as an example of the category wanted. 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier but selects the word's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes a life given over to luxury and pleasure, which is self-indulgent behaviour.

clue.text: Money put aside (not popular) for specialist clothing

indicators.note: not tells us to leave something out of the word

parts.note: money set aside to grow is an investment
something in fashion is in

explanation.surface: Funds saved up, though unpopular, go toward buying uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as an aside, but it is the instruction to drop IN from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a ceremonial robe worn by clergy, so it is clothing for a particular role.

clue.text: Official notes about iron, European

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer letters wrap round the inner

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale, used twice
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European official writes memos about iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Official notes' looks like memoranda, but 'Official' is the definition and the notes are musical ones from do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee is the official who enforces rules during a game, an umpire or judge of play.

clue.text: Instructions about famous work brought over

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: bringing something over flips it, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an epic is a great work, often a long poem or film

explanation.surface: Guidance on a celebrated piece of writing has been carried across from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here supplies letters rather than acting as a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of directions for preparing a dish, so it is a list of instructions.

clue.text: Basic rule about temperature in Swiss region

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is wrapped round another

parts.note: a canon is a fundamental principle
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A basic temperature regulation applies in one area of Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: Switzerland is divided into 26 cantons, such as Geneva and Zurich.
explanation.definitionFit: A canton is one of the federal states making up Switzerland, so it is a region of that country.

clue.text: Lager arranged for scorer

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Beer is laid on for whoever scores the goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' suggests a footballer, but a scorer here writes scores: Edward Elgar, the English composer. 'Arranged' fits music too.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar wrote orchestral scores such as the Enigma Variations, so as a composer he is a writer of scores.

clue.text: Dining, say, having assumed home, first-class, is within reach?

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on board, so the letters are taken inside

parts.note: someone dining is, for example, at table
to be in is to be at home
A is a top grade

explanation.surface: A diner has moved into a first-class home and wonders if it is affordable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At table' is the formal phrase for sitting down to a meal; IN and A go inside it after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attainable can be achieved or obtained, so it is close enough to grasp.

clue.text: Mother's introduction to totem pole

parts.note: Ma is mother, with the possessive s

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Mum is introducing someone to a carved totem pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totem pole' looks like one phrase, but it is split: totem gives a letter and pole is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mast is a tall upright post, as on a ship carrying sails, so it is a kind of pole.

clue.text: Sound of surprise about learner's delight

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is wrapped round another

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
L is the learner driver plate

explanation.surface: A gasp of surprise greets a student's joy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, learner drivers display an L plate, which is why L stands for learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great joy or merriment, which is a synonym for delight in its noun sense.

clue.text: Given to touching diplomacy, yielded at regular intervals

parts.note: tact is diplomatic sensitivity

indicators.note: regular intervals means evenly spaced letters, so every second one is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A touchy-feely negotiator gives ground every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given to touching diplomacy' reads as one phrase, but the definition ends at 'touching'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactile person tends to show affection physically, by hugging or patting, so is inclined to touch others.

clue.text: Diving equipment with edges trimmed for newcomer

indicators.note: trimming the edges cuts off both ends, keeping only the inner letters

parts.note: scuba gear is used for diving; the inner three of its five letters

explanation.surface: Diving gear with its edges trimmed is handed to a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: A cub reporter is a novice journalist, hence the sense of beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A cub is a raw beginner, as in a cub reporter, so it fits newcomer as a noun.

clue.text: A doubly large term in prison — unsurpassed

parts.note: taken as written
L is large, as on clothing sizes, used twice
doing time is serving a prison term

explanation.surface: A convict gets an unbeatable double-length sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A doubly large term' sounds like a long sentence, but A and two Ls are separate pieces before TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record is the best ever recorded, so it is one never beaten or surpassed.

clue.text: Dignity — charm, easily seen in New York

indicators.note: in places one set of letters inside another

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
obi is a West Indian charm or fetish, a variant of obeah
something lit up is easily seen

explanation.surface: Grace and charm are on full view in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' suggests charisma, but here it is a magic object, an obi.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobility of bearing means a noble, stately manner, which is the same quality as dignity.

clue.text: Some hype a nutritious item?

indicators.note: some means only part, so a run of letters is taken from within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word, the next, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Certain people promote a particular healthy snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: some people do talk up this protein-rich snack as a health food.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is a protein-rich legume eaten as a snack, so it is a nourishing food item.
